scope: Separate candidate similarity from identities admitted to semantic consumers, without changing byte/reference candidates.
fixture_note: Isolated Release fixture with the earlier platform-selection, CRC and reference-propagation changes plus the scoped changes reviewed here. Relevant production sources match the review tree. This is not a full build of current dev. CPU/web/Python/Z3 disabled; LLVM 23 r6 and the same Capstone/frozen performance-library inputs as the previous record. The large session, safety and language test files retain the fixture base plus only this change.
signature_revision_note: The updated submodule carries evaluator/collector tooling; no .pat file changed between these revisions. Matching uses the same pattern data on both sides.

host.load_note: Concurrent compiler/research processes were active; this is not an isolated performance certification.

binary_note: The paired timing binaries precede the final call-graph consumer correction. The final CLI quality recheck and SDK tests use the corrected shared library; call-graph construction is outside the measured sigs command. SignatureDB.cpp is unchanged between those builds.

method.accuracy: Normal CLI sigs --auto --sig-base signatures --no-debug --json, eight stripped MSVC compatibility probes. Independent MAP/truth files are read by the evaluator only; no truth names enter the matching process. Every original ordered JSON row remains exactly equal after removing the three additive admission fields.
method.paired_apply: One database and executable, baseline SignatureDB methods linked under distinct symbols and compiled against the current class layout. Two processes per input/worker count; one warmup pair then 21 measured pairs, alternating order. Fixed affinity [4] for one worker and [4,6,8,10] for four. Before: apply + legacy name settlement. After: apply + the same candidate settlement + admitted name map. Loading, discovery, index warmup and result hashing are excluded.
method.paired_summary: Median of the two process medians; every sample retained. Raw match and candidate-name FNV-1a digests agree across every pair. Fixed entry files are the same as the prior reference-check benchmark; normal CLI discovery is evaluated separately.
method.cli: Alternating fresh processes, warm existing parsed-file cache, one warmup pair plus five measured pairs across all eight probes with four workers. Wall/child CPU include the command and /usr/bin/time; maximum RSS is KiB. Output SHA-256 checked against each version of the quality report.
method.cli_control: The two initially slower probes were repeated with one/four workers, one warmup plus eleven pairs. All samples retained; neither trial set was selected for a favorable result.
method.sdk_phases: One C API driver loads either frozen before or after shared library in separate processes; measures image loading, automatic signature application, JSON and destruction; eleven paired samples after warmup.
method.same_binary_diagnostic: A separate non-shipping shared library contains both baseline and current SignatureDB methods; an environment switch selects only apply and refresh-name settlement. The same driver, class layout, loading, discovery and libraries are used. Fifteen pairs after warmup with one/four workers. Scoped CPU/wall timers isolate signature loading (overlaps async function discovery), waiting for entries, pipeline clearing, matching including cold index construction, personalities and name refresh. perf sampling was unavailable because perf_event_paranoid=4; no host setting was changed.

summary.interpretation: All eight stripped probes lack independent identity evidence. The policy abstains from all automatic names, including the correct ones; this is not improved recognition coverage or proof that the false candidates were corrected. Suggestions remain accessible.
summary.performance_interpretation: Warm matching/candidate work remains close in the paired measurements. Initial full-command CPU regressions were not consistently reproducible: x86 four-worker regression repeated in the CLI control, while ARM64 did not. Same-binary phase diagnostics attribute the larger x86 increase to the unchanged signature-load/discovery phase, not matching or name refresh. Concurrent host load prevents a universal end-to-end non-regression claim; retain all measurements and repeat on an idle host for latency certification.

validation.sanitizer_scope: ASan/UBSan on SignatureDB.cpp and SignatureDBTests.cpp only; linked dependencies uninstrumented; mimalloc disabled for this executable.

worker_transport.scope: Standalone mock-backed transport server; no GUI or real worker/engine integration qualification.

validation.format: clang-format 22.1.2 on modified C/C++ files; git diff --check; passed

independent_type_erasure_witness.observation: read_first(First const*) and read_second(Second const*) each contain 8b09e900000000 and the same REL32 relocation to consume at offset 3, despite different nominal source types. Neither full bytes nor that confirmed call can recover the nominal type.

limitations: No common configured cross-tool benchmark; no claim of superiority to other tools.
Compatibility probes are not held-out generalization evidence; no additional real ELF/Mach-O/kernel/mobile naming truth corpus was qualified.
No complete current-dev product build, GUI run, or full-tree sanitizer qualification.
General instruction-normalized fingerprints, independent data/type witnesses and persistent index startup remain separate work.
The existing personality recognizer can admit names through its dedicated context checks; this change does not redesign its already-adopted image metadata lifecycle.
